payload.name: Retrieve Generic Creative Work Descriptions
payload.description: When a question asks what a specific creative work (screenplay, book, film, project) is about, use before hybrid search to also query generic descriptors like 'creative project' and 'completed project' and inspect event/achievement memories.
content: When the user asks about the subject of a specific creative work, do not restrict search to the exact artifact term and ordinal; include query expansions and keywords using generic descriptors such as 'creative project', 'completed project', 'recent work', plus thematic/content words from the question.

If initial results contain no memory stating the completed work's subject, search or inspect event memories with predicates like achievement or completion rather than only in-progress plans or titles, since completed works may be stored generically.

Judge evidence sufficiency against all retrieved current related memories, not only those mentioning the exact artifact type; a memory describing a completed creative project with matching themes can satisfy the question.

solves: Retrieval misses the answer when a memory encodes a completed creative work in generic terms ('creative project') rather than by its specific type ('screenplay'), so a query anchored on 'third screenplay' fails to surface it. Future questions about the subject of any specific creative work should broaden retrieval to generic project/completion descriptors and thematic keywords before concluding evidence is missing.
